headline: Harper's walk-off single beats Mets after Neris blows the save
recap: Bryce Harper singled to right field with one out in the bottom of the ninth, scoring Roman Quinn from second base and giving the Phillies a 6-5 win over the Mets. New York had tied it moments earlier when Robinson Cano's RBI single off reliever Hector Neris brought home Brandon Nimmo in the top half.

Phillies starter Spencer Howard lasted 3.1 innings and allowed four runs, three earned, on seven hits, including back-to-back solo home runs by Dominic Smith and Robinson Cano in the third. Mets starter Walker Lockett went six innings and allowed five runs on seven hits.

J.T. Realmuto's three-run homer in the fifth, scoring Rhys Hoskins and Harper, put Philadelphia ahead 5-4. Neris blew a one-run lead in the ninth but was charged with the win after Harper's walk-off hit.
